entry.title: What Are Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs)?
entry.summary: Historically Black Colleges and Universities are accredited U.S. institutions established principally to educate Black Americans during eras when access to higher education was systematically denied. They remain open to students of all races and continue to play an important role in education, culture, research, and economic mobility.
entry.body: The Higher Education Act defines an HBCU as an accredited college or university established before 1964 whose principal mission was, and is, the education of Black Americans. HBCUs were created in response to exclusion from much of American higher education, especially during and after slavery and segregation. Today, HBCUs include public and private institutions and enroll students from many racial and ethnic backgrounds. Members can use the U.S. Department of Education and NCES links below to find institutions and compare programs, admissions, tuition, and other current information. The Library treats HBCUs as both an education subject and part of the history of Black communities in the United States.
